[element-pub-date]
=== `<pub-date>` Publication Date

In ISO STS, this element holds the date on which a standard is (or was) first published. For this NISO STS Tag Set, this publishing date should be recorded using the <<element-release-date,`<release-date>`>> element.

#### Usage/Remarks
##### Pub Date Deprecated

For new documents, tagging the published date as <<element-release-date,`<release-date>`>> is considered Best Practice. The element <<element-pub-date,`<pub-date>`>> should not be used as part of a standards document’s metadata.
The <<element-pub-date,`<pub-date>`>> element has been retained in the ISO-related metadata elements (<<element-iso-meta,`<iso-meta>`>>, <<element-reg-meta,`<reg-meta>`>>, <<element-nat-meta,`<nat-meta>`>>) for purposes of backwards compatibility. This element has been placed into the models for <<element-std-meta,`<std-meta>`>> and <<element-std-doc-meta,`<std-doc-meta>`>> for purposes of ISO and ISO-related organization’s future migration.
Here is a tagged example from ISO STS of the previous use of the element <<element-pub-date,`<pub-date>`>>:
[source,xml]
....
<iso-meta>
  ...  
  <pub-date>2009-05-30</pub-date>
  <release-date>2009-05-30</release-date>
   ...
</iso-meta>
....
Here is a NISO STS tagged example showing the <<element-release-date,`<release-date>`>> element replacing <<element-pub-date,`<pub-date>`>> for initial publication and description of the current standards document:
[source,xml]
....
<iso-meta>
  ...  
  <release-date 
    date-type="published"
    std-type="new-standard"
    iso-8601-date="2009-05-30">2009-05-30</release-date>
  <release-date 
    date-type="published"
    std-type="IS" 
    iso-8601-date="2009-05-30">2009-05-30</release-date>
   ...
</iso-meta>
....
#### If Publication Date is _Not_ Available

The `<pub-date>` is an optional element, so if the publication date is not available, the element can just be omitted. The preferred replacement element <<element-release-date,`<release-date>`>> is also optional, so if the publication date is not available, both of these elements can just be omitted. However, if the <<element-pub-date,`<pub-date>`>> is unknown (for whatever reason) the word “`unknown`” is allowed to be used as the element content:
[source,xml]
....
<pub-date>unknown</pub-date>
....
